clue.text: Raised support, quietly elated about recruiting son

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: elated recruiting a son takes the abbreviation for son into its ranks
about can mean round and about, so the letters of elated are turned around into a new order

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone in high spirits about a son joining up, with a nod to placing them on a raised support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ELATED once the S taken in by 'recruiting' has joined it, giving EDESTAL after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth on which a statue stands is a raised base or support.

clue.text: Keep quiet, depressed after tweet

indicators.note: after places depressed second, following the word for tweet

parts.note: to tweet is to pipe, as a bird does
depressed means down, low in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone told to hush after a gloomy social media post.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal imperative telling someone to stop talking or be less noisy.

clue.text: Skill required in case of demands for game in pub

indicators.note: required in tells us the skill word must be put inside
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: skill is art, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A pub game where you need skill to cope with what is demanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing arrows at a board is the classic British pub game.

clue.text: Score badly covering hard and unknown piece of music

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of score, with the two added letters, are put together wrongly

parts.note: H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard
Z is one of the algebraic unknowns, like x and y

explanation.surface: A poorly performed musical score that glosses over a difficult, obscure piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' says the rearranged SCORE wraps round H and Z, which end up split within it: SC-H-ER-Z-O.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, often playful movement in a symphony or sonata is a type of musical piece.

clue.text: Liverpool music venue lacking boundaries, say

indicators.note: lacking boundaries strips the venue name of its first and last letters

parts.note: the Cavern Club in Liverpool is where the Beatles made their name

explanation.surface: Talk about a famous Liverpool club losing its limits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cavern Club is the Liverpool cellar venue where the Beatles played early gigs.
explanation.definitionFit: To state firmly or assert something is to say it.

clue.text: Black, and almost identical stuff that's thrown out

parts.note: jet is a deep black, as in jet-black

indicators.note: almost signals dropping the last letter of the word for identical

parts.note: identical means the same

explanation.surface: Black, near-identical rubbish being thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods cast overboard from a ship, washed ashore, are flotsam's companion: discarded material.

clue.text: Even off, cut and wrap

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of even are disarranged

parts.note: to lop is to cut, as with branches

explanation.surface: Trim the edges evenly, cut, then wrap it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose or completely surround something is to wrap it.

clue.text: False modesty mainly protects her, being stifled

indicators.note: protects signals that the shuffled letters surround and shield the next word
false indicates the letters are not genuine, so they are reshuffled
mainly means most of the word, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Feigned modesty shields a woman as she is smothered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False modesty' reads as a phrase, but 'False' is the anagram signal working on the trimmed word; 'being' is just a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stifled is being suffocated or choked, deprived of air.

clue.text: Wealth of men heartlessly collecting shells

indicators.note: collecting means the remaining letters gather the next item inside
heartlessly removes the central letter of men

parts.note: shells are ammunition, informally ammo

explanation.surface: The riches of cold-hearted men amassed by collecting seashells.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical personification of riches and greed, so wealth as an idol.

clue.text: Regular church people first to trace old paper

parts.note: par is the normal or regular level
people means men

indicators.note: first to takes only the opening letter of trace

explanation.surface: Regular churchgoers being first to find an ancient document.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal skin prepared for writing was the historical forerunner of paper.

clue.text: Duck across wet ground keeping nothing for drier

indicators.note: across means the duck spans the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck

indicators.note: keeping means the shuffled letters hold the next item
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of wet are rearranged

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A duck crossing wet ground with nothing, hinting at drying off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drier' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is a noun: something that dries.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for drying dishes is a drier in the kitchen sense.

clue.text: Drive and energy — oddly very low in reverse

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of very
in reverse means the word for low is read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Drive and energy may be very low when going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives VR from very; 'in reverse' turns MOO into OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun for vigour or forcefulness, as well as the noise of a revving engine.

clue.text: Long for free rides across Spain

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters stretch round the next item
free means loose, so the letters of rides are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Yearning for free rides through Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn for or crave something is to want it strongly.

clue.text: Fuss created by welcoming everybody who should be heard

indicators.note: welcoming means the word by takes the next word into itself

parts.note: taken as written
everybody means all

indicators.note: should be heard tells us the word who is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word who, spoken, sounds like hoo

explanation.surface: A commotion caused by a welcome for everyone who deserves a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy publicity or commotion; a song and dance about something.

clue.text: English journalists going in like this coffee

indicators.note: going in means the journalists are placed inside the words for like this

parts.note: so means like this, in this way
journalists collectively are the press

explanation.surface: English journalists heading in for a strong coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like this' gives SO, the word that does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Person looking for opportunities with skipper?

parts.note: windows are opportunities, as in a window for talks
one who skips is a hopper

explanation.surface: Someone seeking openings, accompanied by a ship's captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' looks like a captain, but here it is one who skips, i.e. a hopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser who examines shop displays without buying is someone just looking.

clue.text: Some long, for a change, to adopt international coinage

indicators.note: to adopt means the rearranged letters take in the next item
for a change means the letters of some long are altered in order

explanation.surface: A long phrase is altered to take on an international coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly invented word or expression is a coinage.

clue.text: Suspect Poles will accept America getting support

indicators.note: will accept means the jumbled letters take the next item inside
suspect means dodgy or doubtful, so the letters of Poles are jumbled

parts.note: USA is America

explanation.surface: Suspicious Poles taking in America in return for its support.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting or championing a cause is supporting it.

clue.text: Is he bred for transport by more remote group at sea?

parts.note: more remote means further out

indicators.note: transport means carry elsewhere, so the letters of is he bred are moved around

explanation.surface: Wondering if livestock are bred to be shipped by a distant island group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like shipping, but it signals the rearrangement; the islands lie off north-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of islands off north-west Scotland, a group in the Atlantic.

clue.text: Sailor fetches butts?

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
fetches means gets

explanation.surface: A sailor collecting cigarette ends, or barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butts' suggests cigarette ends or casks; here it means objects of ridicule or aims.
explanation.definitionFit: Butts of jokes are their targets, those aimed at.

clue.text: Gave an account of losing time for kiss, being laid-back

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped and another put in its place

parts.note: to give an account of a story is to relate it
X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: Someone recounting a story, losing track of time over a kiss, quite unbothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and easygoing, at ease rather than tense.

clue.text: High purpose hurt feelings

parts.note: high food has gone off, starting to rot
an end is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: A noble aim that upset people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like lofty, but it means smelly, as with gamey meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone or cause them to feel resentment.

clue.text: Wave from student about teatime approximately? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: about normally means one thing goes round another
quite the reverse swaps the roles, so the time goes round the student

parts.note: teatime is around four o'clock, so approximately four
L is a learner driver's plate, a student

explanation.surface: A student waving at roughly teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as L around FOURISH, but 'Quite the reverse' flips it: FOURISH goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamboyant wave or gesture of the hand.

clue.text: Book bingo getting drunk

parts.note: lotto is a game like bingo

explanation.surface: A book of bingo, and getting tipsy at the bingo hall.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for very intoxicated, legless.

clue.text: Source of tinny hooter that's a cause of irritation

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter, where the word begins

parts.note: a horn is a hooter

explanation.surface: Something with a tinny horn that grates on people.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn in one's side is a persistent annoyance.

clue.text: People who lived in sin casually

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A people who lived together unmarried, in sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-Columbian Andean people of Peru; a member of that nation.

clue.text: European low-fat cream

parts.note: lite is the marketing spelling for low-fat

explanation.surface: A low-fat cream from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The best, the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Offensive old boy confronting Number Ten with evidence of debts

parts.note: X is ten in Roman numerals
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: An unpleasant old boy facing down Downing Street with unpaid bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number Ten' suggests the Prime Minister's residence; it is NO and X separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely unpleasant or objectionable.

clue.text: Daughter needs a face-covering material

parts.note: a mask covers the face

explanation.surface: A daughter needs a face mask made of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A figured woven fabric, usually silk or linen.

clue.text: Detective seen in erotic number

indicators.note: seen in means the detective appears inside the next word

parts.note: carnal means sensual or erotic
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective spotted in a racy song or dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' suggests a song; it means a counting number like one or two.
explanation.definitionFit: A counting number such as one, two or three, as opposed to an ordinal.
